title: Discovery and qualification
summary: Turn broad requests into an agreed problem, evidence and a testable success contract.
outcomes: Ask neutral questions that separate the requested tool from the decision.
Trace data, timing, corrections, identities and ownership through the current path.
Write measurable criteria without inventing a baseline or excluding inconvenient records.
startingAssumptions: A stakeholder statement is reported evidence until its basis is understood.
Cinderline and every number are fictional teaching inputs.
editorialRationale: Each beat develops one mechanism or decision with inspectable inputs. The final changed case tests transfer; preserved canonical lessons provide their original depth and historical anchors.

concepts.definition: A specific recent instance used to understand a problem and its consequences.
concepts.example: Walk through last Tuesday’s disputed quality report.

concepts.definition: A record of affected roles, their decisions, concerns and acceptance responsibilities.
concepts.example: Quality accepts the denominator; security accepts access.

concepts.definition: A precisely defined event used as the start or end of a timing measure.
concepts.example: Approved source record available at 07:00; served at 07:35.

concepts.definition: A description of today’s data flow, rules, constraints and ownership.
concepts.example: Meeting report ← workbook ← ERP extract plus approved correction CSV.

concepts.definition: A label distinguishing observed, reported, proposed or unverified information.
concepts.example: Source family reported; exact CDC permission unverified.

concepts.definition: A pre-agreed condition with metric, threshold, population, time basis and acceptance owner.
concepts.example: At least 95% of all 20 agreed test records meet the timing threshold, with valid timestamps for all.

concepts.definition: Whether required observations exist for every record in the agreed test population.
concepts.example: One of 20 records lacks the source timestamp needed to measure freshness.

concepts.definition: A concise description of affected work, current difficulty, consequence and evidence gaps.
concepts.example: Dispatch decisions wait for approved orders; the actual delay and cause still need measurement.

concepts.definition: A source condition needed for a specific change-capture mechanism, not just for connecting to the database family.
concepts.example: The reviewed setup distinguishes change tracking, which requires a primary key, from CDC; the database name alone does not tell you which mechanism is usable.

concepts.definition: The slower part of a response-time distribution that a single average can conceal.
concepts.example: It hides that one in ten observed refreshes took twenty minutes; report the distribution and the failed or missing observations as well as the average.

concepts.definition: The mechanism by which released resources or capacity become a specific useful outcome.
concepts.example: Time released can increase useful capacity without reducing expenditure; the value claim needs an explicit realization path.

concepts.definition: Learning how a task is actually performed by observing it in its normal setting, with agreed consent and handling.
concepts.example: Record the observed workaround, ask what triggers it and why, and revise the current-state model instead of treating the interview statement as a complete workflow.

selfQuestions.prompt: Rewrite “How much money would our faster system save?” as a neutral discovery question.
selfQuestions.modelAnswer: What work is delayed today, what does the team do instead, and how is the impact recorded?
selfQuestions.reasoning: The revised question does not assume the proposed system is faster or that a financial saving has been established.

selfQuestions.prompt: The sponsor likes the demo. Which approval is still missing if the quality owner has not accepted the denominator?
selfQuestions.modelAnswer: Metric meaning remains unaccepted. The sponsor’s reaction does not establish the correct numerator, denominator or exclusions.
selfQuestions.reasoning: Acceptance follows the relevant responsibility and evidence, not enthusiasm.

selfQuestions.prompt: Which measure changes if the query drops from 2 seconds to 1 second while publication remains 07:35?
selfQuestions.modelAnswer: Click-to-answer latency improves by 1 second. The 35-minute source-availability-to-serving interval remains unchanged.
selfQuestions.reasoning: Improving one clock does not change the events defining another.

selfQuestions.prompt: Why investigate correction identity before choosing a faster ingestion path?
selfQuestions.modelAnswer: Faster transport can deliver the same ambiguous revisions sooner. The system still needs a defensible rule for which business record and revision each event represents.
selfQuestions.reasoning: Transport performance cannot supply missing business semantics.

selfQuestions.prompt: Rewrite “CDC is approved” when the only evidence is an analyst saying it might be enabled.
selfQuestions.modelAnswer: The analyst reports that CDC may be enabled; configuration and permitted use remain unverified with the DBA and security owner.
selfQuestions.reasoning: Enabled, supported and permitted are separate claims, and the note should not imply any is established.

selfQuestions.prompt: What is missing from “the report should be 95% fast” that the worked contract supplies?
selfQuestions.modelAnswer: A defined metric and endpoints, threshold units, population, window, completeness/exclusion rules and accepting owner.
selfQuestions.reasoning: A percentage without a denominator or method is not an interpretable criterion.

selfQuestions.prompt: Can the missing record be called on time because no lateness was observed?
selfQuestions.modelAnswer: No. Absence of a usable timestamp is absence of the required evidence. It fails the completeness condition and cannot enter the on-time numerator.
selfQuestions.reasoning: Unknown is not equivalent to pass or to a measured late value.

selfQuestions.prompt: Write a three-sentence dispatch discovery brief without assuming streaming is the answer.
selfQuestions.modelAnswer: Identify a recent late dispatch decision and trace the order from approval to report to user action. Confirm status semantics, permissions, operating owner and the timing baseline. Agree a population and success criterion, then compare the smallest paths that could meet it.
selfQuestions.reasoning: The brief follows the work and missing evidence before selecting a technology.

beats.title: Start with the last time it happened
beats.outcome: A concrete episode reveals work that a feature request hides.
beats.explanation: “We need real time” names a proposed means. Ask for a recent [[dbxfe-m02-concept-episode|discovery episode]]: who noticed the problem, what decision they could not make, what happened next and what evidence remains. Cinderline’s morning meeting may need a trustworthy number before it needs continuous updates. Neutral questions leave that possibility open.

handbook.markdown:
### Follow an event before offering a solution
Begin with a concrete situation rather than an abstract wish. “When did this last happen?” often reveals actors, timing and workarounds that “what features do you want?” misses. Ask what the person needed to decide, what information was unavailable or disputed, and what they did instead.

For Cinderline, operations says the 08:00 meeting used yesterday’s numbers. That could reflect late source approval, slow processing, a stale dashboard or disagreement about what should count. The episode supplies a path to distinguish these causes. Do not assume a delayed meeting caused a production loss without a causal and measurement basis.

**Worked question:** “Which decision would have changed if the accepted quality number were available by 07:45?” invites a useful answer or an honest admission that the benefit is unproven. “How much would our real-time platform save?” presupposes both the solution and its value.

**Troubleshooting:** acknowledge frustration without converting estimates into observed facts. Summarize the episode back to the stakeholder and preserve corrections. A discovery conversation is not complete simply because a list of questions was asked.

beats.recap: A concrete episode reveals work that a feature request hides.
beats.changeNote: New teaching beat; visiting it does not inherit historical lesson completion.

samajh.text: Doctor ke paas “mujhe yeh medicine chahiye” bolne se pehle symptoms ka recent episode samajhna useful hota hai. Discovery mein bhi “real time chahiye” request hai; last problem kab hui aur decision kya tha, woh samjho. Solution tab actual need se connect hota hai.
samajh.mapping: Requesting a remedy maps to requesting technology; understanding the episode maps to discovery.
samajh.boundary: This is an analogy about inquiry, not medical guidance or a claim that a sales conversation is diagnosis.

beats.title: One word can hide several acceptance tests
beats.outcome: Different stakeholders may mean different things by “good data.”
beats.explanation: A [[dbxfe-m02-concept-stakeholders|stakeholder map]] connects each person’s decision to evidence and acceptance. Operations needs a usable morning number; quality owns its definition; analysts need less reconciliation; security controls the permitted path. Agreement from one enthusiastic person does not settle the others’ conditions. Preserve disagreement so it can shape the test.

handbook.markdown:
### Find the people behind the requirements
Do not treat a [[dbxfe-m02-concept-stakeholders|stakeholder map]] as a list of titles. Ask what decision each person makes, what failure they care about and what evidence would change their view. A sponsor can authorize investment without being able to validate the metric’s numerator. A data lead can validate a transformation without accepting a security boundary.

The fictional example starts with “trust the report.” Operations means available before the meeting. Quality means the approved revision and unit-based denominator. The analyst means a reproducible calculation that does not require manual merging. Security means permitted fields and identities. These are compatible aims, but they need distinct tests.

**Worked action:** invite the quality owner to compare two competing definitions using the same small input. Record the chosen meaning and unresolved historical-restatement policy. Ask operations whether the chosen number changes the decision they described.

**Limit:** a proposed acceptor must acknowledge the role. If a relevant person is absent, keep their condition open rather than writing “all stakeholders agreed.” Discovery is partly the work of making missing participation visible.

beats.recap: Different stakeholders may mean different things by “good data.”
beats.changeNote: New teaching beat; visiting it does not inherit historical lesson completion.

beats.title: Separate three kinds of delay
beats.outcome: Query speed, data freshness and decision timing answer different questions.
beats.explanation: A [[dbxfe-m02-concept-clocks|measurement endpoint]] names where timing starts and ends. Source availability, served-data freshness and click-to-answer latency are different measures. In the synthetic example, a two-second query still returns a report built before the latest approved correction. Optimizing the query cannot make unavailable or unprocessed source data appear.

handbook.markdown:
### Put the clocks on one timeline
Choose timestamps that correspond to the user’s problem. Source event time may precede source approval. Source availability may precede ingestion and publication. A dashboard click happens later still. Label these endpoints rather than calling all of them latency.

In our synthetic example, approval occurs 07:00, publication 07:35, and a user’s query takes two seconds at 07:40. Source-available-to-serving delay is 35 minutes. Click-to-answer delay is two seconds. Neither number alone describes the age of data if the report excludes a later correction.

**Worked investigation:** ask operations whether the missing information was approved before the report cutoff. Ask the data team when it was served. Ask the analyst which interaction was slow. This separates upstream timing from processing and presentation problems.

**Limit:** clocks need consistent time zones and synchronization. Missing timestamps should be reported, not silently excluded. Query profiles can help investigate execution details, but they do not measure the entire business freshness path. The customer must agree which endpoints correspond to the actual decision.

beats.recap: Query speed, data freshness and decision timing answer different questions.
beats.changeNote: New teaching beat; visiting it does not inherit historical lesson completion.

beats.title: Trace one record backward from the decision
beats.outcome: The current-state inventory should reveal rules and owners, not just tools.
beats.explanation: A [[dbxfe-m02-concept-trace|current-state inventory]] follows the report back through transformations, deliveries and the originating record. Ask about identity, revisions, schema, frequency, access and failure handling at each step. Cinderline’s late CSV correction may expose an interpretation problem even when transport is fast. Preserve what is known and who can answer the gaps.

handbook.markdown:
### Investigate one important path deeply
Start with a disputed report and identify the specific records behind its number. Work backward through the calculation, accepted revisions, delivered files and source events. For each boundary ask who owns it, what identity is stable, how ordering is known, and what happens when delivery repeats or arrives late.

The fictional ERP uses persistent inspection IDs, while a CSV may arrive after the first report. If the CSV lacks an authoritative revision, arrival time alone cannot safely determine truth. This is a semantic uncertainty, not merely a connector selection issue.

**Worked inventory output:** SQL Server is reported as the source; its version/topology and permitted privileges need DBA confirmation. Quality must confirm correction order and restatement rules. Operations must confirm when the number is useful. These gaps can change the architecture and test population.

**Troubleshooting:** avoid replacing a missing fact with a generic product claim. A supported database family does not prove compatibility with the exact source setup. Review connector-specific prerequisites, and separately confirm customer permission to enable or use them.

Include corrections in the current-state trace. An inspection corrected after the first extraction changes the accepted unit denominator even when its business date stays the same. A faster ingestion path alone cannot decide which revision is authoritative or when yesterday’s report should be restated.

beats.recap: The current-state inventory should reveal rules and owners, not just tools.
beats.changeNote: New teaching beat; visiting it does not inherit historical lesson completion.

beats.title: Label fact, report and assumption
beats.outcome: The evidence status should survive the meeting notes.
beats.explanation: A [[dbxfe-m02-concept-status|evidence status]] tells the next reader how a statement is supported. “The DBA showed the version” is different from “the analyst thinks CDC is enabled” and “we assume CDC is allowed.” Keep the source, date and validation owner. This lets later corrections update the design without turning an unverified premise into a promise.

handbook.markdown:
### Preserve attribution without dismissing people
A reported statement can be useful evidence. It becomes misleading when the note removes its source or implies independent verification. Use plain labels: observed in a record, reported by a stakeholder, proposed target, or assumption to verify. Retain important disagreement rather than smoothing it into consensus.

For Cinderline, the analyst reports nightly extracts and manual CSV corrections. The source owner has not confirmed the extraction privileges. The architecture note should retain both facts about the conversation. “Incremental ingestion approved” would be an unsupported upgrade.

**Worked ledger:** statement; status; source/date; consequence; next owner. The version check belongs to the DBA, the data classification to security and the metric meaning to quality. Prioritize the uncertainty that can change the next decision rather than treating every gap equally.

**Troubleshooting:** when evidence changes, write the resolution and its impact. Do not delete the original assumption if it explains a prior choice. An honest revision trail is more useful than a note that appears to have known everything from the start.

beats.recap: The evidence status should survive the meeting notes.
beats.changeNote: New teaching beat; visiting it does not inherit historical lesson completion.

beats.title: Write a criterion another person can test
beats.outcome: A threshold needs a population, window, method and acceptor.
beats.explanation: A [[dbxfe-m02-concept-criterion|success criterion]] describes success before the result is known. Cinderline proposes approved one-plant records, valid timestamps, five staffed days and at least 95% served within 60 minutes of source availability. Those are hypothetical targets for agreement. The baseline, exception policy and accepting owners still need to be established.

handbook.markdown:
### Make the denominator and failure rule explicit
“Fast enough” cannot resolve a disagreement after the test. State the timing endpoints, the record population, the window, the threshold and who accepts the outcome. Add correctness and timestamp-completeness conditions instead of assuming the latency statistic covers them.

The fictional proposal measures from approved source availability to serving. It asks that at least 95% of the agreed records meet 60 minutes during five staffed days. This is not a product guarantee or a claim that every record meets the threshold. A proposed target becomes a test contract only when the relevant owners accept it.

**Worked preparation:** collect today’s timing distribution using the same definition; agree treatment of missing timestamps, exclusions, downtime and corrections; then preserve the criterion version. Do not change the denominator after seeing an inconvenient result.

**Limit:** a small sample supports a bounded observation. Even 19 of 20 meeting a criterion does not establish long-term service reliability. Record the count and population alongside the percentage, and distinguish the proposed target, current baseline and observed result.

beats.recap: A threshold needs a population, window, method and acceptor.
beats.changeNote: New teaching beat; visiting it does not inherit historical lesson completion.

samajh.text: Exam ka pass rule pehle clear hota hai: kaunse questions count honge, marks kitne aur passing threshold kya hai. Test ke baad difficult question denominator se hata do toh result misleading ho jayega. Pilot criterion mein bhi population aur exclusions pehle agree karo.
samajh.mapping: Exam scoring basis maps to an agreed measurement population and threshold.
samajh.boundary: A customer pilot is not an exam; business acceptance may include several non-numeric conditions.

beats.title: A missing timestamp is not an on-time record
beats.outcome: Keep unknown evidence in the denominator you agreed.
beats.explanation: The synthetic test has 18 on-time records, one late record and one missing timestamp. Under the agreed all 20 record criterion, only 18/20 are demonstrably on time:90%. [[dbxfe-m02-concept-unknown|measurement completeness]] is also incomplete. Do not drop the unknown to improve the percentage or count it as a pass. Report the two distinct failures and their next investigations.

handbook.markdown:
### Compute what is actually demonstrated
The numerator is the number proven to meet the timing threshold. The denominator is the agreed population, not a convenient subset chosen after the test. Here 18 records are proven on time, one is proven late and one is unknown. Eighteen divided by 20 is 90%. The 95% target is not met, and the all-record timestamp requirement also fails.

Removing the unknown produces 18/19, about 94.74%, which still fails 95% but more importantly changes the agreed basis. Counting it on time produces 19/20 without evidence. Neither operation repairs the missing observation.

**Worked readout:** “On the 20-record population,18 met the timing target, one took 90 minutes and one could not be measured. Investigate the late path and missing timestamp separately, retain the input basis, and rerun after correction.” This is a bounded test conclusion, not proof that the platform can never meet the need.

**Troubleshooting:** distinguish a late data path from a broken measuring instrument. Both affect this criterion, but the owners and repair steps may differ. Preserve the original failed result alongside the later retest.

beats.recap: Keep unknown evidence in the denominator you agreed.
beats.changeNote: New teaching beat; visiting it does not inherit historical lesson completion.

beats.title: Discover a dispatch problem before prescribing streaming
beats.outcome: Carry the questions into a new workflow with different clocks.
beats.explanation: A fictional distributor says dispatch is slow. Apply the same [[dbxfe-m02-concept-transfer|problem statement]]: inspect one late order, separate source approval from processing and screen response, map acceptors and define a bounded test. If orders are released only after a daily approval, faster queries alone may not change dispatch. Let the evidence change the proposed solution.

handbook.markdown:
### Build the brief from answers, not assumptions
The transfer case starts with an unclear request for streaming orders. Ask the dispatch lead for the last delayed shipment and the decision that was blocked. Ask order operations when the order became approved. Ask the data team when the report incorporated it. Ask the user which screen interaction was slow. These questions separate workflow, freshness and interaction latency.

Map the owners: operations accepts dispatch usefulness, order management defines valid status changes, security approves the source path and an operator owns failures. A proposed architecture remains conditional on those inputs.

**Worked first brief:** “Determine whether approved orders can reach the dispatch decision in time. Baseline and source approval cadence are unmeasured. Trace one recent case, agree the status/population and timestamp endpoints, then choose a bounded comparison.” This leaves room for process improvement, a scheduled feed or an incremental path.

**Review entry:** use core cards to rehearse neutral inquiry, current-state tracing and success criteria. Extension cards add concrete connector and measurement caveats. The fictional interview is practice in reasoning, not evidence that a real customer has accepted a requirement.

beats.recap: Carry the questions into a new workflow with different clocks.
beats.changeNote: New teaching beat; visiting it does not inherit historical lesson completion.

extensionCards.prompt: Why ask whether SQL Server tables have primary keys when discussing Lakeflow Connect source setup?
extensionCards.answer: The reviewed setup distinguishes change tracking, which requires a primary key, from CDC; the database name alone does not tell you which mechanism is usable.
extensionCards.explanation: Consider two synthetic source tables in the same SQL Server instance. One has a stable primary key; the other has repeated rows and no key. “SQL Server is supported” does not resolve this table-level difference. Ask the DBA which capture mechanism is permitted, what key and retention properties exist, and which version, topology and privileges apply. The current AWS setup page also lists configuration and access prerequisites. A permitted CDC mechanism would not magically supply a business identity that the source never had; extraction feasibility and downstream record meaning remain separate. Record the missing prerequisite and compare an approved alternative without claiming you configured or executed ingestion.
extensionCards.whyItMatters: It adds a concrete table-level discovery question that a product-family checkbox can miss.

extensionCards.prompt: Nine report refreshes take one minute and one takes twenty. What does a 2.9-minute average hide?
extensionCards.answer: It hides that one in ten observed refreshes took twenty minutes; report the distribution and the failed or missing observations as well as the average.
extensionCards.explanation: The synthetic arithmetic is (9 × 1 + 20) / 10 = 2.9 minutes. A stakeholder waiting for that twentieth-minute result experiences a very different service from the mean. Google SRE explains why latency tails matter and why fast errors must be distinguished from fast successful responses. Ask discovery participants which slow cases matter: month-end volume, a particular plant or a concurrent workload may define a critical subgroup. With only ten observations, do not present an elaborate percentile estimate as statistically settled. Preserve each timing and its outcome, then agree what additional sampling is needed. This adds distribution reasoning beyond simply choosing the correct start and end clocks.
extensionCards.whyItMatters: It reveals recurring painful cases that an apparently acceptable average can obscure.

extensionCards.prompt: Why ask what a saved analyst hour enables, rather than treating it automatically as cash savings?
extensionCards.answer: Time released can increase useful capacity without reducing expenditure; the value claim needs an explicit realization path.
extensionCards.explanation: FinOps unit-economics guidance distinguishes resource measures from business outcomes. In our synthetic case, reconciliation falls from four hours to two, but the analyst remains on the same salary. The direct observation is two hours released, not two hours of payroll removed. Ask whether that time lets the analyst cover another plant, investigate exceptions earlier or avoid planned overtime, and who can verify the result. Each is a different hypothesis with different evidence. Do not add all of them as separate financial benefits if they describe the same two hours. This discovery question sharpens a future value model while keeping the operational improvement useful even when it is not immediate cash savings.
extensionCards.whyItMatters: It connects the proposed efficiency gain to an outcome the stakeholder can actually observe.

extensionCards.prompt: A user says the report is fully automated, but a normal work-session observation shows a manual spreadsheet repair. How should discovery use that?
extensionCards.answer: Record the observed workaround, ask what triggers it and why, and revise the current-state model instead of treating the interview statement as a complete workflow.
extensionCards.explanation: GOV.UK’s contextual-research guide explains observation choices and their tradeoffs. Quiet observation can preserve natural flow but leave actions unexplained; asking every step can clarify intent while changing the activity. In the fictional report session, note when the export is opened, which correction is made and what decision depends on it, then ask the user to explain the exception. Obtain appropriate consent and avoid unnecessary sensitive recordings. One session does not establish frequency across all teams: ask for additional representative cases. The adjacent method adds evidence about workarounds that a retrospective question may miss, without treating either the participant or the observer as infallible.
extensionCards.whyItMatters: It surfaces hidden operating work before the architecture or benefit estimate assumes it away.

recap.title: Carry this forward
recap.markdown: Episode → stakeholders → clocks → record path → evidence status → criterion → honest readout. Keep target, baseline and observed result distinct. Revisit the core cards, then use researched extensions to sharpen a specific technical or value question.

appliedTask.title: Apply the whole module
appliedTask.prompt: A distributor requests real-time dispatch reporting. Draft neutral discovery questions and a proposed timing criterion; explain how you would report 18 on-time,1 late and 1 unmeasured record in a 20-record trial.
appliedTask.modelAnswer: Ask for the last blocked dispatch decision, approval timing, report publication and click response. Confirm order identity/status changes, source permission, acceptors and operator. Propose endpoints, population, window, threshold and missing-data rules for agreement; collect a comparable baseline. Under an all 20-record, at-least 95% criterion with valid timestamps required,18/20=90% is a failure and the missing timestamp is a separate completeness failure. Investigate both without dropping the unknown.
appliedTask.reasoning: The plan avoids prescribing the requested mechanism prematurely and preserves the denominator, evidence status and accepting roles.
